----

Takeaways:

1. AI work is shifting from writing prompts to directing fleets of agents, with judges and adversarial verification making the agents more trustworthy and less prone to hallucination.

2. Individual token prices keep falling, yet total bills rise because agents consume far more tokens per task, so AI compute cost is starting to rival human salaries.

3. Anthropic and Claude now dominate the enterprise market, raising 65 billion at a 900 billion valuation and drawing massive investment from Google, Amazon, and Microsoft.

----

Quotes

"From prompting to directing agents. From capability to trust."

"The engineer of the future is a builder, someone who decides what to make and directs AI to make it rather than writing the code themselves."

"Intelligence solves problems while wisdom chooses which problem to solve."

----

Summary:

In this Friday AI update I walk through dozens of developments. 

Claude Opus 4.8 launches as the new default with a fast mode and dynamic ultra-code workflows that spawn many parallel sub-agents verified by judges. 

Cursor releases its Composer 2.5 coding model, and cheaper Chinese models and DeepSeek discounts push token prices down even as overall usage and costs climb past employee salaries. 

I cover harness engineering, MCP tunnels, using cheaper sub-agent models, and tools like Hermes, ECC, OpenClaw, and OpenSpec. 

On the business side, Anthropic raises record funding and dominates enterprise, Google invests heavily, and companies flatten org charts and cut jobs as AI takes over routine work. 

I also touch on quantum-informed AI, robots, Obsidian for memory, and solo founders building profitable AI-run businesses.
